- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (forecast > true by >10%) — apply downward correction of 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- Overshoot in early forecast window (first 5–7 days) — reduce forecast by 3–8% if sentiment is positive but trending downward.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is weak or negative.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops below 0.15 after 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 3–7% to account for delayed market reaction.
- Avoid overconfidence in high-sentiment periods — cap forecast increase to 3–5% above recent 10-day average unless sentiment > 0.45.
